players.note: Bucky Irving is the RB16 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.8 touches and 87.6 total yards. Irving has a 64.7% snap rate, a 59.6% rushing share, and a 47.7% route share (10.8% target share). Among 39 qualifying rushers, he is 24th in explosive run rate and 15th in missed tackle rate. Irving should post RB1/2 numbers this week with a wonderful matchup. Carolina has allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, the second-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 11th-highest missed tackle rate.

Chase Brown is the RB19 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19 touches and 74 total yards. In his last game before the bye, Samaje Perine did cut into his early-down workload, but I'm not concerned about Brown moving forward. In that game, Brown still had a 60.3% snap rate, a 41.9% rushing share, and a 60.6% route share (12.5%) target share. He did split the red zone rushing work with Perine, with each back seeing four red zone rushing attempts, but Brown had a 63.2% snap rate in the red zone. I think Brown's workload could bounce back this week, but even if it continues along this path, he is still the workhorse back for Cincy. Among 38 qualifying backs, Brown is 19th in yards after contact per attempt and 27th in missed tackle rate. Brown will have to get by with passing game usage and overall volume this week after laying all of that out because Baltimore's run defense has been formidable this season, allowing the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the 11th-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Woody Marks finished with 17 touches and 81 total yards with a 77.8% snap rate. He should be Houston's workhorse again this week. Marks also had a 60% route share and 8.8% target share. Marks was the RB22 for the week. Among 39 qualifying rushers, Marks is 14th in yards after contact per attempt and ninth in missed tackle rate. Marks should be a strong RB2 this week with RB1 upside. New York has allowed the third-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest rushing success rate, and the ninth-highest yards after contact per attempt.

Saquon Barkley will be back this week. In his two full games this season, he has averaged 16 touches and 80 total yards with RB29 and RB30 finishes in weekly scoring. Barkley has posted a strong 11.8% explosive run rate and 22% missed tackle rate this season. With the Eagles' injuries to their pass-catching depth chart, Barkley could be leaned on heavily this week. Since Week 3, the Cowboys' run defense has improved, allowing the eighth-lowest rushing success rate, the seventh-lowest missed tackle rate, and ranking 16th in yards after contact per attempt allowed. Behind an offensive line that, since Week 3, has had the sixth-lowest yards before contact per attempt, Barkley might not find much running room this week.

Braelon Allen could be the Jets' workhorse back again this week, but it's also possible that Breece Hall is back this week. If Hall is out, then Allen is an RB1/2. If Hall plays, Allen is only a flex play. Let's discuss Allen's outlook if Hall is out because if he plays, Allen is likely only an 8-10 touch play and you're praying for a touchdown. Since Week 4, Allen has been the RB23 in fantasy points per game, averaging 20 touches and 95.6 total yards. In those three games, Allen has had an 88% snap rate, 75.3% of the rushing work, and a 64% route share (10.7% target share). Among 39 qualifying rushers, Allen is 11th in explosive run rate, seventh in yards after contact per attempt, and tenth in missed tackle rate. Allen could run wild this week. Miami has allowed the eighth-highest rushing success rate, the second-highest zone rushing success rate, the 12th-highest zone yards per carry (Allen: 59.5% zone), and the fourth-lowest stuff rate.

Rhamondre Stevenson remained New England's lead back last week, but TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner cut into his early-down workload. Stevenson played 60.3% of the snaps with a 42.9% route share, but he had only 38.9% of the rushing work. Stevenson finished with 14 touches and 36 total yards. Overall, he has averaged 14.3 touches and 62.3 total yards this season. Among 38 qualifying rushers, Stevenson is 17th in yards after contact per attempt and 11th in missed tackle rate. Stevenson should return RB2 value this week. Chicago has allowed the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the seventh-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards before contact per attempt.

Josh Jacobs will be back this week. He practiced all week and doesn't carry any injury designation into this game, but his workload is a question. I HIGHLY doubt he will be Green Bay's clear workhorse in his first game back, but he'll likely take a sizable chunk of passing downs, factor in on early downs, and be the guy in the huddle in the red zone. He could easily see 10-12 touches this week and save his fantasy day with a touchdown. Jacobs at least returns to a plus matchup. Detroit has allowed the fifth-highest explosive run rate, the tenth-highest rushing success rate, and the fifth-most yards before contact per attempt.

In his two games as the Dolphins' starting running back, Ollie Gordon has averaged 14.5 touches and 94 total yards as the RB16 and RB14 in weekly scoring. In those games, he had a 63.4% snap rate, 51.9% of the rushing attempts, a 46.3% route share, and a 4.5% target share. He should be Miami's lead back again this week. Among 39 qualifying rushers, Gordon is fourth in explosive run rate and yards after contact per attempt. Gordon should post another nice stat line this week. The Jets' run defense has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest rushing success rate, and the 12th-highest missed tackle rate.

With Jordan Mason back this week, I'm expecting Aaron Jones to split the work with him as they did in Week 1. Aaron Jones can't hold up to this bellcow role that he has had without Mason. Jones has also been gutting it out on one good knee weekly. If Minnesota REALLY wants to make a playoff run this season, they need Jones healthy for the rest of the season. In Week 1, Jones had a 42.6% snap rate, 35.3% of the rushing work, a 23.3% route share, and a 4.2% target share. Jones finished with 12 touches and 40 total yards (one score). In that game, Jones and Mason split the red zone work with each back seeing four red zone rushing attempts. Indy has allowed the seventh-highest rushing success rate, the third-most yards before contact per attempt, and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate. Jones and Mason could each flirt with 10-15 touches in this game and get into the end zone as they did in Week 1.

Since Week 2, Tony Pollard has been the RB34 in fantasy points per game, averaging 17.4 touches and 67.8 total yards. During that span, he has had two RB2 weekly finishes (RB16, RB24). Across his last five games, he has had a 56.9% snap rate, 68.4% of the rushing work, a 30.6% route share, and a 5.5% target share. Among 39 qualifying backs, Pollard has been solid, ranking 15th in yards after contact per attempt and 21st in explosive run rate. If Cam Ward can provide somewhere in the vicinity of decent quarterback play and move the offense, Pollard could be an RB2 again this week. Cleveland's run defense has been horrible, allowing the second-highest explosive run rate, the 12th-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

J.K. Dobbins is the RB37 in fantasy points per game with two top-24 weekly finishes this season (RB13, RB15). Dobbins has averaged 14.8 touches and 49.5 total yards. He has a 43.9% snap rate, a 55.1% rushing share, and a 16.3% route share (4.2% target share). Among 39 qualifying backs, Dobbins is 28th in explosive run rate, 23rd in yards after contact per attempt, and 35th in missed tackle rate. Dobbins could be an RB2 again this week. Arizona has allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards after contact per attempt, and the second-highest missed tackle rate.

RJ Harvey has quietly been a top-24 running back in weekly scoring in three of his five games (RB24, RB12, RB13) this season. Harvey has averaged 8.8 touches and 48.8 total yards, with the bulk of his production coming in the passing game. Harvey has a 15.8% target share, 2.30 YPRR, four red zone targets, and a 10.8% first-read share. Arizona has the highest rate of two-high in the NFL (69.8%). Against two high, Harvey has had an insane 41% TPRR with 2.32 YPRR. He should see PLENTY of targets this week. Harvey is a strong flex again this week against an Arizona defense that has allowed the 11th-most yards per target to running backs.

I have zero confidence in starting anyone from the Seattle backfield right now. Last week, Emanuel Wilson lost his lead back role as he played only 32.9% of the snaps while having 53.8% of the rushing attempts and only a 13.8% route share (one target). If Seattle is playing from behind in this game, Wilson could see his role eaten up by George Holani, who had a 56.1% snap rate last week. Last week, Wilson finished with 14 touches and 52 scoreless rushing yards. Among 38 qualifying backs, Wilson is 26th in explosive run rate and 25th in missed tackle rate. Kansas City has allowed the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, I was expecting Tyler Allgeier to be Arizona's bell cow back, but it didn't happen. Last week, he played 55.6% of the snaps, finishing with 19 touches and 48 total yards. Allgeier had 51.4% of the rushing attempts, a 48.6% route share, and a 2.9% target share. Allgeier and Bam Knight split the red zone work equally, with each back seeing four red zone rushing attempts. Allgeier hasn't been impressive as a rusher this season with only a 4.1% explosive run rate and 9% missed tackle rate. If Allgeier sees similar volume again this week, even if he's not efficient with it, he's still on the flex radar. Denver has had issues stopping the run this season, allowing the sixth-highest explosive run rate, the most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

Quinshon Judkins has practiced on a limited basis all week (ankle). He'll be back this week and should lead the Browns' ground game. Judkins is the RB20 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.2 touches and 60.6 total yards. Among 39 qualifying rushers, Judkins is 35th in explosive run rate, 31st in yards after contact per attempt, and 22nd in missed tackle rate. Judkins gets quietly an amazing matchup this week. Tennessee's run defense has been a dumpster fire since Week 3, allowing the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the tenth-highest rushing success rate, and the 12th-highest zone rushing success rate (Judkins: 57.5% zone).

With Jordan Mason back in the huddle this week, I'm expecting a split of the workload similar to what we saw in Week 1. In Week 1, Mason had a 47.5% snap rate, 44.1% of the rushing work, and a 23.3% route share (zero targets). Mason finished with 15 carries for 59 rushing yards (one score). Mason was the RB23 for the week. In that game, Jones and Mason split the red zone work, with each back seeing four red zone rushing attempts. Indy has allowed the seventh-highest rushing success rate, the third-most yards before contact per attempt, and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate. Jones and Mason could each flirt with 10-15 touches in this game and get into the end zone as they did in Week 1.

Alvin Kamara has been a limited committee back over the last two weeks, averaging seven touches and 37.5 total yards. Since Week 5, he has played only 25% of the snaps with an 18.2% rushing share and a 17.2% route share (10.9% target share). Yes, he has three scores across his last three games, but we can't count on a touchdown to save his fantasy day weekly. Kamara is a weekly sit until his role changes in the New Orleans backfield.

The Saints' backfield has dissolved into a gross three-way committee with Kendre Miller handling the bulk of the early-down work. Last week, he finished with 22 touches (20 carries) and 70 total yards. He had a 45.6% snap rate, 52.6% of the rushing work, and a 15.6% route share (6.7% target share). With the early-down volume, Miller is a viable flex option again this week. Miller's per-tough rushing efficiency has been putrid, though. He has only a 2.4% explosive run rate, 1.73 yards after contact per attempt, and a 12% missed tackle rate. If the Saints are playing from behind this week, Miller could easily get gamescripted out of the Week 7 action, so that also has to be added to his volatility. Pittsburgh hasn't been an imposing run defense, allowing the 14th-highest explosive run rate, the 11th-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 14th-highest missed tackle rate. Miller needs the Saints to play with a lead this week and a touchdown to likely pay off for fantasy purposes. Both are questionable propositions in Week 7.

Blake Corum has played 23-29.1% of the snaps in four of six games this season, while averaging 9.3 touches and 52.4 total yards. Corum's added passing game usage has been a nice wrinkle this season. He has at least two targets in each of his last four games, with two games with at least four targets. With Davante Adams out, I wouldn't be shocked if the Rams leaned on their strong running game even more. Over the last two weeks, Corum has been the RB13 and RB10 in weekly scoring. Among 38 qualifying backs, he is sixth in explosive run rate and 14th in missed tackle rate. Corum should have another strong week against the Raiders' run defense, which has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate while having the 13th-lowest stuff rate and sitting at 15th in missed tackle rate.

Roschon Johnson has been solid over the last two weeks. Over the last two games, he has had a 39.7% snap rate, a 31.6% rushing share, and a 34.1% route share (11.8% target share). He has averaged 12.5 touches and 62.5 total yards with RB31 and RB15 finishes in weekly scoring. Johnson hasn't been impressive on a per-touch basis with only 1.82 yards after contact per attempt and a 14% missed tackle rate. New England could allow him to flirt with strong flex value again this week. New England has allowed the 11th-highest rushing success rate, the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 17th-highest missed tackle rate.

I was shocked last week by how involved Bam Knight was. He played 44.3% of the snaps, had 42.9% of the rushing attempts, and logged a 28.6% route share (5.7% target share. Knight finished with 17 touches and 98 total yards. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight split the red zone work equally, with each back seeing four red zone rushing attempts. Knight had a 20% explosive run rate, 2.14 yards after contact per attempt, and a 17% missed tackle rate last week. All of those are solid to very impressive numbers. Knight was the RB20 in weekly scoring last week. He could have another strong week against Denver. Denver has had issues stopping the run this season, allowing the sixth-highest explosive run rate, the most yards after contact per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

I don't want to start anyone from the Giants' backfield this week. I have no clue how the coaches divide up the workload this week, even without Najee Harris. Last week, Cam Skattebo didn't have a touch, and he played only six offensive snaps. Last week, Devin Singletary, Tyrone Tracy, and Najee Harris all played at least 15.3% of the snaps and had at least 20% of the rushing work. Singletary led the group with a 39.6% route share. This backfield could be a mess this week, and the matchup is so tough I don't see any back having a great day when the volume could be capped. Houston has held rushers to the third-lowest explosive run rate while posting the tenth-highest rate of backs hit at the line of scrimmage or behind it and the fourth-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Rico Dowdle returned to the field last week. He finished with ten touches and 49 total yards. Dowdle had only a 27.6% snap rate, 31.8% of the rushing work, and a 13% route share (6.1% target share). Jaylen Warren is the clear backfield leader now. Dowdle did split the red zone work with Warren, with both backs having a 45.5% red zone snap rate and one red zone rushing attempt last week, so he does still have some touchdown equity in this offense. That and the wonderful matchup put Dowdle on the low end of the flex radar this week. New Orleans has allowed the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, and the ninth-highest missed tackle rate.

In his last game before the bye, Samaje Perine finished with 16 touches, 78 total yards, and a score as Chase Brown's backfield running mate. I'm not willing to declare Perine as a standalone flex play moving forward, as that was the first game of the season where Perine had more than eight touches. In that Week 5 game, Perine played 50.8% of the snaps with 45.2% of the rushing volume, but he had only a 33.3% route share. He did split the red zone work with Brown, as each back had four red zone rushing attempts, but Brown dwarfed him in snap rate (63.2%) inside the 20-yard line. That feels like more noise than signal of Brown's role being in serious jeopardy moving forward. I'm not flexing Perine this week in a matchup that is rough on paper for early down production. Baltimore is allowing the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the 11th-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, TreVeyon Henderson had only a 23.5% snap share, a 19.4% rushing share, and a 20% route share (3.1% target share). Henderson finished with eight touches and 40 total yards. Corey Kiner cut into his early-down load. I expect Henderson to flirt with 8-10 touches again this week as a middling flex with a good matchup. Among 38 qualifying backs, Henderson is 28th in yards after contact per attempt and 31st in missed tackle rate. Henderson likely needs a score to pay off this week, but if he rips off a big run, he could get it. Chicago has allowed the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the seventh-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards before contact per attempt.

Jonah Coleman will be back this week. He practiced in full all week (ankle). Sean Payton stated that Coleman will be on a snap count in his first game back, so it's impossible to plug him into a lineup this week. I'm high on his rest-of-season outlook, but I can't trust him in fantasy this week.

Breece Hall opened this week with a DNP, but he managed limited practices on Thursday and Friday. He has been listed as questionable. He could easily be back on the field this week. If he is active, I expect him to reclaim his lead back role as an RB2 with Braelon Allen sprinkled in. In Weeks 1-2, he averaged 22.5 touches and 105 total yards. Hall was the RB13 and RB12 in weekly scoring in those weeks. Among 39 qualifying backs, Hall is 16th in explosive run rate and 23rd in missed tackle rate. Braelon Allen could work in more than we saw in those first two games of the season, but I expect Hall to still lead the backfield in touches this week (if active). Miami has allowed the eighth-highest rushing success rate, the second-highest zone rushing success rate, the 12th-highest zone yards per carry (Hall: 54.9% zone), and the fourth-lowest stuff rate.
